questions.q: What are the three kinds of principal Unity Catalog recognizes in a GRANT statement?
options: Users, groups, and service principals
Users, roles, and policies
Workspaces, catalogs, and schemas
Admins, editors, and viewers
questions.explain: A GRANT's TO clause always names a user, a group, or a service principal — the only three principal types Unity Catalog recognizes.

questions.q: How is a user identified in a GRANT statement?
options: By their account email address
By an internal numeric user ID only
By their workspace display name
By a randomly generated UUID
questions.explain: Users are identified by their account email address, e.g. GRANT SELECT ON TABLE t TO `alf@melmak.et`;

questions.q: How is a service principal identified in a GRANT statement?
options: By its applicationId, a UUID — not an email address
By the email of the engineer who created it
By its Databricks cluster ID
Service principals cannot be granted privileges directly
questions.explain: A service principal is represented by its applicationId value (a UUID), enclosed in backticks, unlike a human user's email.

questions.q: Why use a service principal for a scheduled job instead of a human user's credentials?
options: So the automation's identity and access don't break or over-reach when the person who wrote the job leaves or changes credentials
Because service principals run jobs faster than human accounts
Because Unity Catalog does not allow human users to own jobs
Service principals are required only for jobs that process more than 1TB of data
questions.explain: A service principal is an identity independent of any one person, scoped to what the automated process needs, avoiding breakage or stale over-broad access tied to a human's credentials.

questions.q: What does the built-in `account users` group represent?
options: Every user on the account — granting to it is the broadest possible grant
Only workspace admins
Only service principals, never human users
A group that must be manually created before use
questions.explain: `account users` is a built-in group including literally every user on the account; it ships with Unity Catalog and doesn't need to be created.
